name: Grafana
tagline: An observability platform for dashboards, metrics, logs, and alerting.
hook: A Go and TypeScript guide to local instructions, test skills, generators, environment differences, deployments, and compatibility.
summary: Grafana's root guide maps its Go and TypeScript monorepo and points specialized work to local instructions and testing skills. Schema and service edits have generators; PATH and test-runner behavior vary by environment.

techniques.title: Derive change boundaries from deployment boundaries
techniques.body: Frontend and backend changes are assigned separate PRs because they ship on different cadences. The storage notes extend that reasoning to independently deployed services that need compatibility in both directions.
techniques.quote: Separate PRs for frontend and backend changes (deployed at different cadences)

techniques.title: Route visualization tests through an additional guide
techniques.body: All frontend testing follows one skill, with panel and visualization code loading another on top. The shared guide defines the default and the specialization without treating every frontend change identically.
techniques.quote:
Write tests for new functionality — for frontend code, use the `frontend-testing-strategy`
  skill for this repo's testing conventions (and `panel-testing-strategy` on top of it for
  visualization/panel code)

techniques.title: Tie schema changes to both generated languages
techniques.body: The CUE schema note explains that a schema edit produces Go and TypeScript output. Service initialization, feature flags, and Go workspace membership have their own named generation commands.
techniques.quote: **CUE schemas**: Dashboard/panel schemas in `kinds/` generate both Go and TS code via `make gen-cue`.

techniques.title: Turn an interactive test default into a one-shot command
techniques.body: The cloud-environment section warns that the normal frontend test command watches by default. It provides both a direct Jest invocation and a flag that let an automated run terminate.
techniques.quote: **Frontend tests**: The `yarn test` script includes `--watch` by default. Always use `yarn jest --no-watch` or add `--watchAll=false` to run tests once and exit.

steal: Explain how deployment cadence constrains the scope of a change.
Layer specialized test guides on top of shared ones.
Name every language affected by schema generation.
Document interactive command defaults that would leave automated work waiting.
